prov.heading: CREDIT LOSS EXPENSE (BENEFIT)
prov.text:
The Company had credit loss expense of $601 million and $1.3 billion for the three months and nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to credit loss expense of $368 million and $1.2 billion for the corresponding periods in 2025. The higher credit loss expense during the three months and nine months ended September 30, 2026 was primarily due to the acquisition of Webster this quarter and a higher reserve release in RICs and auto loans during the prior periods.

Credit loss expense on commercial loans increased $77 million and increased $90 million for the three months and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to the corresponding periods in 2025 primarily due to the acquisition of Webster.

Credit loss expense on consumer loans increased $121 million and increased $13 million for the three months and nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the corresponding periods in 2025. This was primarily due to the acquisition of Webster this quarter and a higher reserve release in RICs and auto loans during the prior periods.

The credit loss expense on unfunded credit losses for the three months and nine months ended September 30, 2026 increased $35 million and increased $10 million compared to the corresponding periods in 2025 primarily due to the acquisition of Webster.

net.text: To mitigate interest rate risk and, to a lesser extent, foreign exchange, equity and credit risks, the Company uses derivative financial instruments to reduce the effects that changes in interest rates may have on net income, the fair value of assets and liabilities, and cash flows.

ocf.heading: Cash flows from operating activities
ocf.text: Net cash flow from operating activities increased by $2.6 billion from the nine months ended September 30, 2025 to the nine months ended September 30, 2026, primarily due to the change in net trading activity and an increase in proceeds from the sales of and collections on LHFS, offset by an increase in originations and purchases of LHFS during the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

da.text: • Lease expense decreased $131 million and $323 million for the three months and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to the corresponding periods in 2025, due to lower auto lease volumes resulting in lower depreciation expense.

Net interest income.heading: NET INTEREST INCOME
Net interest income.text:
Overall, the increase in net interest for the three months and nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the same period in 2025 was primarily driven by higher loan and investment securities volumes, coupled with reduced funding costs on securities financing activities and borrowings and other debt obligations. These positive impacts were partially offset by lower deposit-related income. The net result reflects the combined effect of balance sheet repositioning and higher market interest rates during the period.

intro.text: SHUSA is the parent holding company of SBNA, a national banking association; SC, a consumer finance company headquartered in Dallas, Texas; BSI, a wholly-owned subsidiary of SBNA, a financial services company headquartered in Miami, Florida that offers a full range of banking services to foreign individuals and corporations based primarily in Latin America; SanCap, an institutional broker-dealer headquartered in New York which has significant capabilities in market-making via an experienced fixed-income sales and trading team and a focus on structuring and advisory services for asset originators in the real estate and specialty finance markets; SSLLC, a broker-dealer headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts; and several other subsidiaries. SHUSA is headquartered in Boston and SBNA's home office is in Wilmington, Delaware. SSLLC is a registered investment adviser with the SEC.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Debt securities
lines.why: Bonds held for sale or to maturity: financial.

lines.name: Equity securities
lines.why: Shares held for their return: financial.

lines.name: Loans, net of the allowance
lines.why: Lending is a bank's business: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Long-term debt (incl. current portion)
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans, current maturities included: financial.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
